name: PadButton
meaning: Bit layout of the pad word tested by Pad_MenuPressed/Held/Repeat, which take the INVERTED mask (Pad_MenuPressed(0xBFFF) tests bit 0x4000). Recovered from the masks used across this module; it is exactly the PlayStation digital-pad layout, which the PC port kept. Bits 0x2000 CIRCLE and 0x8000 SQUARE are confirmed in game by the level-skip cheat input.

name: PAD_L3
meaning: InputMgr::Poll binding 10 clears 0xfffd; standard PS1 pad bit 1 (the named bits already follow the PS1 layout: SELECT 0, UP 4 .. LEFT 7, TRIANGLE 12 .. SQUARE 15) (inferred)

name: PAD_START
meaning: binding 9 clears 0xfff7; PS1 pad bit 3; ScnControllable::ReadPad PRESSED(pad, 9) -> WolfActionBits 4 (inferred)

name: PAD_L1
meaning: Input_ApplyControlConfig passes 0xfbff as the 6th remap in every preset; PS1 pad bit 10 (inferred)

name: PAD_CIRCLE
meaning: mask 0xDFFF. Confirmed in game: the 5th/6th press of the level-skip code

name: PAD_SQUARE
meaning: mask 0x7FFF. Confirmed in game: the 1st/2nd/4th press of the level-skip code

name: PAD_ALL_RELEASED
meaning: the raw active-low pad word with no button down (Cheat_CheckSequence tests cur/prev != 0xffff)
